That summer the grass grew so tall that Ántonia and I could lie in it and see nothing but sky. We spent the long afternoons among the gophers and the grasshoppers, telling each other stories in two languages, neither of which the other quite understood. She taught me the names of things in her mother’s tongue — bread, water, sun — and I taught her mine. At evening we walked home through the red light, the windmill creaking on the ridge, and her grandmother would be standing at the door with a lamp. It seemed to me then that the world was very large and very kind, and that nothing would ever change.
